title: Statement Separation and Line Continuation
subtopics: Semicolons and when to avoid them
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of statement separation and line continuation in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply statement separation and line continuation in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to multiline expressions and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Statement Separation and Line Continuation through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding statement separation and line continuation helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Statement Separation and Line Continuation helps you reason about newline handling. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Newline handling. Then connect it to Semicolons and when to avoid them. The remaining syllabus points—Multiline expressions—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.
